title: Amazon MSK & Apache Kafka
summary: Managed Kafka for teams that already use Kafka APIs, provisioned or serverless.
tldr: **Amazon MSK** runs open-source Apache Kafka for you: AWS provisions and patches brokers, replicates across AZs and replaces failed nodes. Existing Kafka producers and consumers work with **no code change**.
**MSK Serverless** removes broker sizing and storage management entirely; capacity scales with throughput. Pick it when the question says "don't provision brokers or plan capacity".
If the scenario already uses Kafka, answer MSK. Moving to Kinesis means rewriting clients, so it fails "no code change" requirements.

keyFacts.text: The durable topic recipe: three replicas across AZs, writes need two in-sync copies, so one broker or AZ can fail without losing acknowledged data.
Provisioned MSK can move older log segments to a low-cost tier while keeping hot data on broker storage. Consumers still replay with standard Kafka APIs.
MSK provisioned supports IAM access control, mutual TLS and SASL/SCRAM. MSK Serverless uses IAM access control.
Managed Kafka Connect workers that run source and sink connectors (for example an S3 sink) without servers to operate.

keywords.cue: replicate Kafka topics to another Region

traps: Adding brokers does not protect a topic with replication factor 1; each partition still has one copy.
`acks=1` acknowledges after the leader writes, so a leader failure can still lose data even with replicas.
Archiving to S3 with a sink connector breaks the requirement to replay with **Kafka APIs**; tiered storage keeps the data in the topic.
SQS, SNS and Amazon MQ for RabbitMQ do not speak the Kafka protocol, so they are wrong for "no code change" Kafka migrations.
